Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old woman with several months of painful, dry, cracked skin on the palms with itching, affecting work as a hotel housekeeper. Suspected dermatitis/contact dermatitis related to occupational exposure; plan includes trigger avoidance, topical corticosteroid, and emollients with short-interval follow-up.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Palmar dermatitis/contact dermatitis with dryness and cracking.
- Onset: started ~3–4 months ago; gradually worsened; currently painful and limits work.
- Associated symptoms: itching; occasional bleeding with scratching; no spontaneous bleeding reported.
- Affected area: palms (mainly).
- ROS: denies fever, nausea, vomiting; no urinary or bowel symptoms; overall well.
- Social history/medications: works as hotel housekeeper; exposure to cleaning products; gloves not consistently worn; changed jobs ~4 months ago; medications include metformin (see PMH).
- Examination findings: not formally documented; description includes dry, cracked palms and pruritus.
- Differential/notes: dermatitis or contact dermatitis; irritant contact dermatitis; potential eczema in differential.

Issue 2:
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- Timeline/PMH: known; on metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: none.
- Social history: non-smoker; light alcohol use (a couple pints per week).
- Examination: not detailed in transcript.
- Plan: no diabetes-specific management changes documented in the visit.

Issue 3:
- Generalized dry skin (xerosis) of legs.
- Timeline: present; described as dry but not severe.
- Symptoms: mild dryness in legs; not a major issue.
- Social/medications: none additional.
- Examination: not detailed beyond patient report.

Medications:
- Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- No known drug or other allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Diabetes mellitus type 2.
- No prior skin conditions diagnosed (eczema/dermatitis not previously diagnosed).

Social History:
- Occupation: hotel housekeeper; exposures to cleaning products; inconsistent glove use.
- Living situation: not specified.
- Smoking: no.
- Alcohol: couple of pints per week.

Preventative History:
- Not documented in transcript.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals not provided.
- Skin findings described verbally as dry, cracked palms with itching; no other systemic exam details provided.

Plan:
- Advise trigger avoidance: wear gloves at all times when cleaning; consider reducing contact with irritants.
- Initiate treatment for dermatitis: topical corticosteroid (steroid cream) for inflammation; stronger emollients to be applied generously 3–4 times daily.
- Follow-up: reassess in 10–14 days (1–2 weeks); if not improved or if worse/spreading, return sooner.
- Prescription: I will generate a prescription for the topical steroid and emollient and send to the pharmacy.
